reason: The 101-row base patch becomes embedded layer files: admin.yml and core.yml (the kernel every profile stacks first) and base.yml (product host-plane services). Its 22 model-facing rows move into the shipped presets, so no host-plane layer mounts a model-facing component. Telemetry, vendor log upload and account sign-in are mounted off or gated.

The browser layer becomes web.yml, which mounts the listener, authentication, routes, stream and page components and the reload entry. The 65 client rows, the gateway rows and the desktop-only analytics rows have no Go counterpart, the 22 disabling overrides are not needed because the agent plane is only in presets, and the glue plugin that prints the URL and opens the browser is area A18's host.launch component.

The package is split. Its runner, flag parser and JSON stream are specified by area A24 as the component cli.headless in areas/app-cli.md and are not redefined here. This area keeps the 46-line patch as headless.yml: it mounts that runner, limits the secret store to environment sources, disables the authorization entry and removes the question tool from the presets.

The patch becomes sdk.yml, which mounts area A20's wire.stdio and wire.sdk components and disables the title model call. The start-up provider that accepted the command line and bound end of input to shutdown is folded into A20's stdio component and A21's launch data. The office-kit, runtime-download and client rows are not carried: office tools are preset children that work only where LibreOffice is installed.

The patch becomes acp.yml, which mounts area A20's wire.stdio and wire.acp components, disables the title model call and removes from the standard preset the children ACP cannot express. The start-up provider is folded into A20's stdio component. The second model default of the upstream row is dropped; the default in the core layer applies.

A minimal SDK profile is kept, but as a subset and not as a second complete tree: profile sdk-minimal stacks the core bundle, the minimal bundle and the sdk bundle. The same capability set also ships as the preset minimal in every other profile, which is what area A24 asked for. Sandbox mode stays workspace-write by default and the vendor session-log row is not carried.

The registry is kept as the component agent.presets with service key agentpreset.Key: eager activation, broken declarations that stay listed, revisions retained by leases, selection only while a session is blank, and the session record. Changed: the realm of a revision is built automatically from declared provides instead of hand-written isolate groups audited for leaks, and every binding is logged with a digest.

The declaration row is kept as the component agent.preset. Its child list becomes a map keyed by child id inside the entry's config, so a layer merges into one child, and a declaration may extend another. The packaged dsh-doc skill directory, located upstream by Node module resolution, becomes an embedded harness-docs skill addressed by name and mounted by the creator preset.

Kept as the component agent.persona: it registers a scoped persona prefix and suffix that shadow the global ones for one preset, a complete-prompt mode and suppression of optional runtime context, through the prompt service of area A03. Added: suppression of named contexts. It still refuses to load outside a preset.

A custom profile in Go extends a built-in profile and has only its own layer, so it cannot omit the bundle that mounts the ACP server (boot.md, DH-ADR-BOOT-1). The carrier entry acp-server is on the required-entry list, so a carrier that fails to load stops start-up with a report instead of leaving a client waiting. An explicit removal of the carrier by a later layer is raised as a request to area A21.

No third-party code runs inside the host: plugins are separate processes whose standard output is their own protocol pipe. In the host, standard output is claimed once by area A20's stdio component, logging and the start-up report go to standard error, and a composition test of A20 forces every logger on and checks that every line is a frame.
The acp profile still reads its configuration once: it does not mount the boot.reload entry, so a layer edit takes effect at the next start.
justification: A reload that restarts a spine entry unloads the ACP server and the agents first, and the restarted server would have to claim standard input and output a second time, which the stdio component grants once per process. The operator can add the reload entry in the profile layer at that risk. Stage DH-S-0 is a placeholder until the implementation plan assigns the stage of DH-D-BUNDLE-3.

reason: A layer operation may merge into an entry's config, so an override changes one field and keeps the rest. The shipped mode layers and the user's profile layer no longer restate whole settings blocks.

The rule that a per-surface default must live whole in the surface bundle followed from whole-config replacement. With merge, a mode layer states only the field that differs (for example headless.yml merges the secret sources) and the shared row stays in core or base.

The bullet describes how the Windows sandbox grants a private temporary directory per session. That behaviour is the contract of area A10 (areas/sandbox-ssh.md) and is unchanged by how layers are composed; the core layer selects only the sandbox mode.
justification: A layer cannot change what the Windows backend can confine; the private temporary directory is the intended confinement and belongs to area A10's specification. Stage DH-S-0 is a placeholder until the implementation plan exists.

reason: The conflicting pair no longer exists: area A08 makes the fence part of the one file operation service instead of a second provider that replaces the first. In general, two enabled entries that provide one service are found by the static check from the catalogue's declared provides before anything starts, and reported for that entry instead of failing the profile at load.
A headless run is still one task and then an exit. A later run continues the conversation with the session option, and area A24 adds an option that runs one human command instead of a task.
justification: One task per process is the contract a supervisor relies on: the exit status is the outcome of that task. Multi-turn driving is the SDK profile's job. Stage DH-S-0 is a placeholder until the implementation plan exists.

reason: Area A13 appends a job's settlement before its owner's final flush, the runner of area A24 waits for the agent and its descendants to be idle and flushed, and boot unloads the tree leaves first inside a bound. A job still running at exit is stopped and its settlement is recorded with the cause, so the interval is closed in the log.

There is no separate start-up row that a composition could disable: the headless layer mounts one runner, which parses its own words, and it restates no policy row. A composition that changes the sandbox policy entry merges fields and does not have to re-wire start-up values.

Area A10 changes the upstream rule that only file tools honour extra roots on Windows: extra roots apply to spawned processes as well, so a run with an added directory no longer fails at the first tool call. This document also asks area A24 to check each added directory against the resolved policy before the first model request.

The limit exists because the upstream bundle is an npm package that another embedder could mount without the launcher that provides the exit request. The Go harness is one binary with one way to start a profile, and the exit request is a launch service that always exists.
Area A24's runner writes reasoning and tool progress to the diagnostic stream but does not promise a line before the first model token, so a slow first token can still look like silence.
justification: The runner is specified by area A24 and not by this document; a progress line at step start is listed as a request to A24 in section 10. Stage DH-S-0 is a placeholder until the implementation plan exists.

reason: Area A24's runner still sends reasoning to the diagnostic stream by default, so a supervisor that keeps standard error keeps model output.
justification: The runner is specified by area A24; this document asks it for a switch that keeps reasoning off the diagnostic stream and cannot add one itself. Stage DH-S-0 is a placeholder until the implementation plan exists.

reason: The result stream still carries only the final answer; intermediate tool output appears only in the JSON mode. Area A24 generalises this as its output contract for every command.
justification: Kept on purpose: a pipeline that reads standard output must receive exactly the answer. The JSON mode, which is now the complete event log, is the way to see everything else. Stage DH-S-0 is a placeholder until the implementation plan exists.

reason: One clause is removed and the others are kept. A session recorded under a preset is no longer refused, because every profile composes presets and the recorded one is bound. A session from another working directory, a subagent session and a session whose lease another process holds are still refused.
justification: The working-directory rule protects the sandbox roots, which derive from that directory; a subagent session is owned by its creator; the lease rule is what keeps one writer per session. Stage DH-S-0 is a placeholder until the implementation plan exists.

reason: The capped projection is not built. Area A24 specifies the JSON mode as every committed session event of the run in area A05's export line format followed by one result line, with no string cut and no event omitted, so the stream is the log.

The sdk profile still starts no web server, so file cards and opening a file need the embedding program. Narrowed: several processes may share one home, so a web host on the same home lists and shows the sessions an SDK host wrote.
justification: The sdk profile exists to be driven by a program over standard input and output; mounting a listener in it would give an embedding program a network surface it did not ask for. Stage DH-S-0 is a placeholder until the implementation plan exists.

reason: The SDK protocol of area A20 still carries no user time zone, so the clock context of an SDK session cannot name the user's zone.
justification: A layer cannot supply a fact the protocol does not carry. A time-zone field on the SDK protocol is requested of area A20 in section 10. Stage DH-S-0 is a placeholder until the implementation plan exists.

reason: A question from the model still needs an answerer: when the SDK client registered none, area A17 settles the call as unavailable with the reason, which is the Go form of upstream's NO_PROVIDER result.
justification: With nobody to ask, the answer is no by design (outcome DH-O-7). Whether the question tool should be hidden from the model when no answerer is bound is asked of area A17 in section 10. Stage DH-S-0 is a placeholder until the implementation plan exists.

reason: A schedule is still delivered only while some host process runs on the home; area A13 reports occurrences missed while none ran instead of replaying them.
justification: The harness has no background service; delivery needs a process. A schedule created in an SDK session is stored in the shared home, so any later host on that home delivers the next occurrence. Stage DH-S-0 is a placeholder until the implementation plan exists.

reason: A custom profile in Go extends a built-in profile and cannot omit the bundle that mounts the SDK server, and sdk-server is a required entry, so a carrier that fails to load stops start-up with a report instead of leaving the client's initialization without a peer.

No third-party code runs inside the host, so an inserted plugin cannot write to the host's standard output: a plugin is a separate process with its own pipes. Standard output is claimed once by area A20's stdio component and all logging goes to standard error.

Saved changes still belong to one profile of one home, so two embeddings that use the same home and profile share them. The second half of the bullet, about the Python launcher needing Node and pnpm, cannot arise: no package manager is involved.
justification: A profile layer is shared state by definition. An embedding that wants its own composition names its own profile (a custom profile is one small file that extends sdk) or its own home, and per-launch overlays change nothing on disk. Stage DH-S-0 is a placeholder until the implementation plan exists.

reason: The sdk profile still reads its configuration once: it does not mount the boot.reload entry, so a layer edit takes effect at the next start.
justification: A reload that restarts a spine entry unloads the SDK server and its agents, and the restarted server would have to claim standard input and output a second time, which is granted once per process. Stage DH-S-0 is a placeholder until the implementation plan assigns the stage of DH-D-BUNDLE-3.

reason: The minimal profile still omits the product services on purpose: it is the core bundle, the minimal preset and the SDK carrier. It is now a subset of the full profile and not a separate tree, so adding one service is one insert in the profile layer.
justification: Being small is the purpose of the profile: an embedding or evaluation run gets an explicit kernel, and the profile proves the spine runs without product services (DH-ADR-BUNDLE-2). Stage DH-S-0 is a placeholder until the implementation plan exists.

reason: Reading an image still needs a model route that accepts images; on a text-only route the tool returns an error. Images are stored through the attachment store of area A07 instead of a fixed directory.
justification: The limit is a property of the selected model, not of the composition. Whether the tool is hidden when the route takes no images belongs to areas A08 and A04. Stage DH-S-0 is a placeholder until the implementation plan exists.

reason: The command registry is part of the core bundle and the minimal preset mounts the compact command, and area A20's SDK protocol runs a recognised command through its query method. An SDK client of the minimal profile can therefore run the compact command; compaction settings are still changed in a layer.

A user layer can only name compiled-in components and plugin processes. Neither can write ordinary text to the host's standard output: host logging goes to standard error, standard output is claimed once by the stdio component, and a plugin process has its own pipes.

The limit exists because upstream's frontend is a JavaScript bundle that must be built before the server can serve it. The Go user interface is rendered by the host from templates and assets embedded in the binary, so there is no separate build to forget.

Half is removed and half is kept. Area A18's listener re-reads the certificate files when they change, so a renewed pair no longer needs a restart. The harness still obtains and renews nothing, and TLS is still something the operator turns on.
justification: Obtaining certificates would add an ACME client, outbound requests and a renewal duty to a local tool, against the rule that nothing leaves the machine by default. The web layer sets no TLS default because a loopback listener needs none. Stage DH-S-0 is a placeholder until the implementation plan exists.

reason: Area A18 refuses a non-loopback bind at start-up unless TLS is configured or the operator sets an explicit insecure-remote flag, which warns at every start. The web layer leaves the bind on loopback and the flag off, so the external leg is never plain HTTP by default.

The host still knows only that it asked the operating system to open a browser. Area A18 does see the launch token being exchanged, which shows that some browser signed in, but not that the hand-off itself succeeded or that the browser later exited.
justification: An operating-system launcher returns before the browser shows anything, and no portable call reports the outcome. The printed URL stays as the manual fallback. Stage DH-S-0 is a placeholder until the implementation plan exists.

reason: Under SSH the URL is still printed and no browser is opened, as area A18's decision table for print and open states.
justification: A browser opened on the remote machine cannot reach the user's screen, so the forwarding client must open the address. This is a physical limit, not a missing feature. Stage DH-S-0 is a placeholder until the implementation plan exists.

reason: The browser override is still taken only from the inherited process environment and never from a discovered environment file.
justification: Kept as a security rule: a file found in a project directory must not choose a program for the host to start. Area A21 refuses launch-affecting names in discovered files for the same reason. Stage DH-S-0 is a placeholder until the implementation plan exists.

reason: A wildcard bind is still refused: area A18 accepts one concrete address literal, loopback by default, and the web layer sets none.
justification: Kept as a security rule: whoever reaches the listener with a launch URL is the owner and can run commands, so binding every interface is never a default or an accident. Stage DH-S-0 is a placeholder until the implementation plan exists.

reason: Two of the three clauses are removed. Configuration can no longer execute host code: children name compiled-in components and expressions are side-effect-free reads, although a preset is still not a security boundary. A user override no longer replaces the whole child list: children are a keyed map that layers merge into, so a later shipped child still reaches that user. Kept: a revision is process-local, so after a restart a session binds the current definition.
justification: A running revision is live component state and cannot be stored. The Go design records the change instead of hiding it: every binding is logged with a digest, and a resume that finds a changed definition appends a new record (DH-ADR-BUNDLE-6). Stage DH-S-0 is a placeholder until the implementation plan assigns the stage of DH-D-BUNDLE-4.

reason: The three statements stop being runtime surprises. A declaration without the registry, a duplicate preset id, an unknown base and a bad child are static issues with file, line and column, found before anything is applied. Declarations still offer no directory or file operations, which is intended: a preset is configuration and its assets are embedded and addressed by name.

The persona component can still be mounted only inside a preset. Mounted at the top level it fails to load, now with a message that names the prompt component's persona field, which is where a deployment-wide persona is set.
justification: Area A03 keeps one owner per prompt fact: the global persona is a live field of the prompt component. A second global owner would make the persona depend on which entry loaded last. Stage DH-S-0 is a placeholder until the implementation plan assigns the stage of DH-D-BUNDLE-5.

reason: The persona config gains a list of context names to suppress, applied through the prompt service's suppression by name, so one optional contributor can be turned off for a preset without turning off all of them. Required contexts, such as the working directory, still cannot be suppressed, and naming one is a load error.

The live event becomes the typed notify key agentpreset.Selected, a scoped event dispatched with the session's scope key after the durable agent-preset/selected event commits. Its payload is the session id, the preset, the digest and the cause; consumers drop state derived from the session's composition.

The schema becomes the Go struct agentpreset.Declaration: ID (required, unique), Name, Description, Order, Extends, and Children as a map from child id to component, disabled switch and config. The upstream plugins list becomes that map, and each child's config is decoded strictly against its component's type by the declaration's validator.

The schema becomes the Go struct agentpreset.Config with Default (required, checked against the declarations as a static issue) and SelectedDefault (a live field saved through the config service of area A21).

No config struct replaces it. The task, session id, output mode, permission preset and approval policy are words of the command line that area A24's cli.headless component parses with its own option specification; the upstream row existed only to carry those values from the start-up provider to the runner.

The schema becomes the Go struct persona.Config: Prefix (required), Suffix (empty), Complete (false), IncludeRuntimeContext (true), plus the new SuppressContexts list of context names checked at load.
The schema's one field named the profile for help text. In Go the profile name is launch data (launch.profile) provided before the tree, and the sdk layer mounts no start-up row that would need it.

The glue plugin is not built in this area. Opening the browser, printing the URL and the advertised public URL are fields of area A18's launch and listener config; the surfaceContext switch becomes whether the web layer registers the DSH_WEB_URL variable with the shell environment component.

ctx.agentPresets becomes the service key agentpreset.Key with interface agentpreset.Service: List, Resolve, Default, Acquire, AcquireFrom, Of, Select, Lookup and Inventory. A lease object replaces the user counter, and Lookup replaces serviceFor.

No service replaces it in this area. The parsed command-line values stay inside area A24's cli.headless component; if a config field must read one of them, that component declares an expression view in the catalogue, as boot.md describes for carrier start-up values.

ctx.webApp offered one method, the advertised URL. That value is owned by area A18's host.launch component, which prints it, opens it and exposes it; the web layer mounts that component instead of a bundle-owned service.

Read in full. Kept: every launch mode is a profile, layers are an explicit ordered list applied over an empty root, only directly listed bundles contribute, and boot and the config dump share one composition function. Changed: a bundle is a named list of layer files embedded in the binary, not an npm package, and a profile is a compiled-in definition plus one layer file. Dropped with npm: pnpm-managed profile dependencies, two-anchor module resolution and the template copy.

Read in full. The ownership rule is kept: a service whose state is per process, or that a component outside the preset reads, belongs to the host plane, and the token meter is one. It becomes a check: a preset child that would write to a shared registry breaks the revision. The note's second decision is changed: joining a preset is part of agent creation in every profile, so an agent without a preset is an error instead of a silent agent with no tools.

Read in full. Kept: a preset is ordinary loader configuration, the registry owns each revision, activation is eager, a failed declaration stays listed and rejects new bindings without stopping start-up, agents and children retain the revision they joined, and the session log records the preset identity. Changed: an override merges into a keyed child map instead of replacing the list, the isolated realm is built automatically, edits go through the one config edit path, and each binding is logged with a digest.

Read in full. Kept as written: the headless layer limits the secret store to environment sources and disables the authorization entry, so a job never reads, migrates or changes saved keys and sign-ins, and the other profiles keep the stored-first order. With merge the layer states one field instead of disabling three rows.
